title: Road to the IGF: Subset Games' Into the Breach
label: developer
claim: Enemies telegraph their moves, 'turning each match into a kind of puzzle'; telegraphed attacks were adopted as 'a core mechanic'; with every attack telegraphed and little random chance, 'it's very clear how or why you failed so that you can feel like you can improve.'

title: Road to the IGF: Zachtronics' Opus Magnum
label: developer
claim: 'It's satisfying to watch factories work, and especially so when it's one of your own design'; animated-GIF export lets players share solutions; several metrics to optimize (cost, area, cycles). The page says nothing of timelines or histograms.

title: PC Gamer: Perfectly solving Opus Magnum's puzzles is impossible
label: snippet
claim: Solutions are scored on measurable traits shown against other players' (histograms); the game's looping GIFs drew attention; 'tall' vs 'deep' solutions.

title: Review: Slay the Spire (LessWrong)
label: opinion
claim: 'Slay the Spire's central innovation is enemy intents.' 'Each turn, you can see what each enemy is planning to do'; over time the player learns each enemy's patterns; later play is 'all about having a plan'; the act's final boss is shown at the start of each act.

title: How to Read Enemy Intent in Slay the Spire 2
label: practitioner
claim: Attack icon carries damage and hit count, shield icon for block, a separate icon for buffs/debuffs; the sequel puts several intents side by side.

title: Slay the Spire's metrics-driven approach (GDC 2019 preview)
label: snippet
claim: Only a talk preview: metrics from early development and through Early Access. Nothing on intent or UI. The talk itself (GDC Vault, gated) was not read.

title: Why RimWorld sold more than 1 million copies
label: practitioner
claim: Quotes Sylvester's book: 'the human mind sees stories anyway, given the slightest of suggestions'; quotes a Reddit AMA: the aim is not for the player to restrict every colonist to the optimal thing. Nothing on mood or inspector design; the apophenia term is the blogger's, from Rock Paper Shotgun.

title: GDC 2017 RimWorld talk listing
label: snippet
claim: Talk covers leaving features out so players engage with story elements not actually there. Fetch 404; seen only in search results.

title: FFXII's gambit system was like programming for beginners
label: practitioner
claim: Gambits are a numbered list, 1 highest priority to 12 lowest, indexed on the left; red commands offensive, blue defensive; 'like we are scripting our own AI allies'. Says nothing on any indicator of which gambit is acting.

title: Choose What's Included in 'Alt' vs. Always On (Factorio forum)
label: verbatim
claim: Players: 'Once you enable ALT mode you rarely disable it'; asks for per-layer choice like the F4/F5 debug options; recipes on machines help them look different, modules are clutter; one player turns alt mode off to spot idle machines. No developers posted.

title: Overlay suggestions and criticisms (Klei forums)
label: verbatim
claim: Fetch 403. Seen in search: ONI has one overlay per system on hotkeys (oxygen F1, power F2, temperature F3, plumbing F6); one player calls the temperature overlay nearly useless.

title: Friday Facts #361 - Train stop limit, Tips and tricks
label: developer
claim: Tips and tricks began to explain things not explained elsewhere; 'The iconic example is the Alt-mode tip. Playing without Alt-mode is painful, and even more painful to watch, so we had to tell the player somehow.' Rule for tips: entities and items should explain themselves through direct means such as entity tooltips; tips cover things not tied to one item (alt info, ghost building) and only things players actually do not get.

title: Friday Facts #351 - Beacon re-redesign & Simplified fluid mixing
label: developer
claim: Beacon redesigned to take less attention; its modules now drawn on the entity, so 'we could remove Alt-mode from the Beacon'; Alt-mode overlay 'isn't really useful most of the time on Beacons', removing clutter; the team does not want a precedent of visible module slots on every entity.

title: Friday Facts #426 - Resource search & assembler GUI
label: developer
claim: Assembler output slot tooltip showed recipe info, hiding the item's spoilage; split so recipe icon/name shows the recipe tooltip and the product slot behaves like every other inventory slot (item tooltip, Alt-click opens the item). Separates 'concerned with the recipe' from 'concerned with a specific item'.

title: Friday Facts #337 - Statistics GUI and Mod Debugger
label: developer
claim: Statistics GUI was a style update only; hovering and highlighting on graphs had been added earlier; exact amount label moved inside a thicker progress bar; a search box added and the team debated how Ctrl+F should pick between production and consumption frames.

title: How RimWorld fleshes out the Dwarf Fortress formula
label: developer
claim: Sylvester's theory: 'create a simulation that was not overly complex, and that a player can observe and comprehend.' RimWorld 'is also abstract, but it shows enough that it constrains the imagination a little bit.' 'The real engine of story is the gameplay systems themselves.' Does not discuss the mood or thought interface.

title: Dwarf Fortress on Steam: the look panel (PCGamesN)
label: practitioner
claim: Panel is 'subdivided intelligently into categories like Relations, Thoughts, Needs', with an Overview tab as 'a nice snapshot of the highest priority information'; works while the game runs, so you 'view a dwarf's thoughts as they have them, in real time'. The page does NOT say it fails to explain actions (an earlier note attributed that to it; unsupported).

title: Tarn Adams on the Dwarf Fortress Steam release (Game Developer)
label: developer
claim: The new UI was done by Zach and Tarn with art contributors; 'an actual UX person take a look later on (later than we should have, not a mistake we're planning to make with adventure mode)', producing the building menu and other smoothing. 'Do not design for your experienced players' is called well-entrenched wisdom; new player experience was the main focus for 2-3 years.

title: Road to the IGF: Slay the Spire (Giovannetti)
label: developer
claim: Developer interview covers card design, combos, path choice and enemy variety; it never mentions intent icons. Null for developer reasoning on intents.

title: Extended Play: How FFXII's Gambit Created One of the Most Distinct RPGs Ever (PlayStation Blog, 2017)
label: developer
claim: Kato: real-time combat added to FF's command battles risked being 'too fast-paced and difficult', 'so to solve this problem we adopted the Gambit system'; grew from FFIV's monster-AI mechanic. Katano/Ito: hard to judge whether it would work until the end. Nothing on how the interface shows which gambit fired (null).

title: PC Gamer: Everything you need to know about Into the Breach
label: practitioner
claim: Matthew Davis: 'Part of our vision for Into the Breach is a push to be more deterministic in the moment-to-moment gameplay.' Writer: 'no fog of war and no percentages'; the Vek 'show you their intended attack and give you a chance to respond before they execute it.' Justin Ma: 'We wanted to come up with something that would be fun regardless of the AI.'

title: Kotaku Splitscreen: Into the Breach creators (GDC 2019)
label: developer
claim: Podcast excerpt on cutting most early systems and nearly giving up; Davis was the playtest 'gut check'. Nothing on telegraphing or UI.
